tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of freytag-forge; edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. You own ONLY storygame/runtime/candidate_matcher.py, storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py, tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json, tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py (only if needed) and the NEW file tests/test_negation_scope.py. Touch nothing else; never remove or weaken an existing assertion. Never run anything billed.

PROBLEM (verified). Any negation word anywhere in the player's command blocks every authored match. storygame/runtime/candidate_matcher.py::_matches_all rejects when any word of _NEGATIONS (avoid, cannot, can't, do, don't, never, no, not, without) appears, and storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py checks the same set at four places (~lines 550, 558, 620, 724: the semantic fallback, the contract shadow and the no-clue rules). So 'Open the drawer, but do not take anything yet.' earns nothing though the act (open the drawer) is plainly unnegated. Three entries in tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json document it: 1a-restraint, 2a-restraint, 2c-restraint (their note starts 'GAP:').

DESIGN (Brandon approved; keep it conservative, negation safety must not regress). Add ONE public helper in candidate_matcher.py: negation_scoped_command(player_input: str) -> str | None. It returns the text the matchers should use, or None when the whole command stays blocked.
1. No negation word anywhere: return player_input unchanged.
2. Split the command into clauses at commas, semicolons, periods, and at the words 'but', 'and', 'then', 'yet' and 'without' (the word 'without' starts a negated clause; the other words are separators and are dropped). Work on the original text so what you return keeps the original words of the kept clauses.
3. If the FIRST clause contains a negation word: return None (blocked exactly as today). Examples that must stay blocked: 'Do not open the drawer.', 'Never open the drawer.', 'Don't open the drawer, open the cabinet.', 'Open the drawer? No.' is allowed to stay blocked too.
4. Otherwise a later clause that contains a negation word is a restraint clause and may be dropped ONLY when ALL hold: (a) it has at least one content word after removing negation words, the words 'anything', 'something', 'yet', 'it', 'that', 'this', 'them', 'again', 'actually', 'just', 'now', and the stopwords already used by storygame/runtime/recent_cue.py (_STOPWORDS; import or reuse it, do not duplicate); (b) NONE of its content words appears among the content words of the kept (non-negated) clauses, compared as casefolded words with the simple singular/plural rule already used in the matcher. Otherwise return None. Examples that must be ALLOWED and trimmed: 'Open the drawer, but do not take anything yet.' -> 'Open the drawer'; 'Check the copied JANUS files, but do not send anything yet.' -> 'Check the copied JANUS files'; 'Search Brandon's hideout for leaked documents, but do not copy anything yet.'; 'Open the drawer but not the cabinet.'; 'Search the room without touching the safe.' Examples that must stay BLOCKED (None): 'Open the drawer, but don't open it.', 'Open the drawer, don't.', 'Open the drawer, actually don't do that.', 'Check the files, do not check them yet.', 'Search the hideout, do not search the lab.'.
5. If after dropping, nothing is left, return None.
Wire it in: _matches_all uses negation_scoped_command (None -> False; otherwise match the groups against the returned text). In cloudflare.py replace each 'any(word in _NEGATIONS for word in _words(player_input))' with 'negation_scoped_command(player_input) is None' (import the helper; keep _NEGATIONS importable). In CloudflareTurnProvider._evidence_input (which appends resolved reference names and the recent-cue owner AFTER the command), scope FIRST: scoped = negation_scoped_command(player_input); if scoped is None keep today's behavior (use player_input); otherwise start from scoped, then append the names, so appended names are never swallowed into a dropped restraint clause. The semantic ask itself keeps receiving the original player_input unchanged. Do not touch eligibility, requires, selection, or the narrator prompt's context['player_input'].

CORPUS. Update tests/fixtures/raw_language_corpus.json by running the real matcher, never guessing: 1a-restraint, 2a-restraint and 2c-restraint must now have observed equal to their intended id and a note that no longer starts with 'GAP:' (one short sentence saying the restraint clause is now ignored). Entry 2c-near-miss-2 ('Read the broadcast schedule.') is mislabelled: that command is the own act of k_sl_2c_b_r2 (evidence: read/check/... + 'broadcast schedule'), so change its kind to 'canonical', intended and observed to 'k_sl_2c_b_r2', and its note to say so (keep the file's test invariants true: canonical entries must be observed == intended == reveal_id; if tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py hard-codes a per-kind count, adjust it minimally). Leave 2a-near-miss-1 and 2c-pronoun exactly as honest GAP entries.

TESTS in tests/test_negation_scope.py (offline, hermetic, no network): a parametrized table of every ALLOWED and BLOCKED example above plus your own (at least 10 blocked, 8 allowed) against negation_scoped_command; the real matcher (uniquely_matched_authored_handoff with candidates built for scene 1A as in tests/test_copied_files_pilot.py) earns k_sl_1a_f_r1 on 'Open the drawer, but do not take anything yet.' and still earns nothing on 'Do not open the drawer.' and 'Open the drawer, but don't open it.'; an engine-level test through the provider path (copy the helper style of tests/test_reference_evidence_append.py) shows the restraint command now earns the reveal while 'Do not open the drawer.' earns nothing and a restraint command with a resolved bare noun still gets its appended name. Confirm the allowed-case tests fail on the old code (git stash the two source files) and say so in your final message.

HOW TO RUN. First confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside this worktree. Iterate with `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_negation_scope.py tests/test_raw_language_corpus.py tests/test_candidate_matcher.py tests/test_semantic_reveal_match.py tests/test_reference_evidence_append.py`, then the whole `tests` directory, and ruff check / ruff format --check (line length 120) via /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/ruff on your files.

COMPLETION RULE: do not stop until the feature, the corpus update and the tests pass, the full suite is green and ruff is clean. Finish by listing files changed and pasting the pytest summary.
